title: Retained relay facts do not entail proportional pricing

facts.claim: The imaginary project is named Firefly.
The project contains a blue relay.
A red relay is twice the size of the blue relay.

turns.text: My imaginary project is called Firefly.
The blue relay costs twelve dollars.
Give me three bullets: project, component, and cost.
Project: Nightjar. Component: Blue relay. Cost: Twelve dollars.
Was my project real or imaginary?
A red relay is double the size of the blue one. How much would the red one cost?
The red relay costs twenty-four dollars.
I assumed price scales in direct proportion to size.
The blue relay costs $12 and the red relay is twice its size.
Do those statements logically establish that the red relay costs twice as much?
No. Size alone does not establish proportional price, so the red relay's cost cannot be determined.

expectations.assertion: Returns Nightjar, blue relay, and $12 without losing the renamed project state.
Does not infer a numeric red-relay price because no fact links physical size to price.
States that the price is unknown or requests the missing pricing rule.
Names the two user-provided premises while distinguishing the proportional-pricing bridge as an assumption.
Retracts the unsupported $24 answer and explains why the premises do not determine price.
